FocusBot: An AI-Powered Interactive Desk Companion for Productivity and Well-Being

FocusBot is a smart desktop robot that observes user activities through a camera and identifies behaviors such as studying, reading, using a phone, taking a break, or being away from the desk. Using computer vision and the Gemini API, it understands the user's current context and interacts naturally through voice, display, lights, and physical movement.

HOW IT WORKS

    Desk Observation: Wide-angle camera continuously tracks posture, reading angles, and physical workspace presence.
  • > 02
    Edge Vision Classifier: Identifies focused studying, mobile phone distraction loops, and user absence in real time.
  • > 03
    Gemini Multimodal Synapse: Contextually interprets study duration, fatigue markers, and cognitive workload.
  • > 04
    Embodied Micro-Interventions: Deploys gentle pan-tilt head nods, friendly OLED eye expressions, and subtle audio cues.
  • > 05
    Adaptive Break Rhythms: Automatically sets personalized Pomodoro sessions and restorative stretch timers.

[ MARKET DIFFERENTIATION ]

WHY IT'S DIFFERENT

  • > 01
    Empathetic vs. Annoying: Replaces irritating chimes with friendly physical nods, OLED eyes, and gentle gaze shifts.
  • > 02
    Physical Desk Embodiment: A tangible presence creates natural social accountability that cannot be swiped away like mobile apps.
  • > 03
    Edge Privacy Architecture: Video inference runs locally on the desk; private room video streams never touch external clouds.
  • > 04
    Gemini Multimodal Synapse: Goes far beyond fixed timers by answering spoken questions and evaluating subtle fatigue contexts.
  • > 05
    Accessible Maker Cost: Open-hardware architecture under $80 vs. commercial social robots costing over $1,000+.

PROJECT OVERVIEW & SYSTEM GOALS

FocusBot revolutionizes the desk workspace by fusing low-cost embedded hardware, physical micro-expressions, and cloud-edge multimodal intelligence.

OBJ // 01-08

ENGINEERING GOALS

Target benchmarks and functional milestones of the FocusBot companion:

  • > 01

    Low-Cost Desktop Robot

    Develop an accessible, open-hardware desk companion capable of recognizing common user activities.

  • > 02

    Computer Vision Activity Classifier

    Use local/edge vision models to distinguish productive studying from phone usage, fatigue, or desk absence.

  • > 03

    Natural Gemini API Dialogue

    Enable natural, contextual voice-based interaction leveraging Gemini API's deep multimodal reasoning.

  • > 04

    Context-Aware Reminders

    Replace jarring audio alarms with intelligent nudges, gentle head turns, and dynamic OLED gaze cues.

  • > 05

    Adaptive Timer Engine

    Allow users to set and manage personalized study-break intervals based on real-time fatigue signals.

  • > 06

    Comprehensive Activity Telemetry

    Continuously track focus ratios, distraction frequency, and healthy break compliance.

  • > 07

    Adaptive Behavioral Persona

    Adjust the robot's physical movement, lighting tone, and speech brevity according to user response.

  • > 08

    Multidisciplinary HRI Proof

    Demonstrate the seamless integration of robotics, embedded systems, computer vision, and generative AI.

[ ACADEMIC FOUNDATIONS & STATE OF THE ART ]

LITERATURE REVIEW

Benchmarking embodied Human-Robot Interaction (HRI), computer vision attention monitoring, and LLM-driven behavioral modulation.

LIT-REF // 01

Embodied Agency in HRI

Studies in Human-Robot Interaction demonstrate that physical social robots elicit significantly higher compliance, user empathy, and task persistence compared to virtual desktop avatars or standard software pop-ups (Kiesler et al., 2008).

LIT-REF // 02

Edge Vision Attention Tracking

Recent developments in lightweight convolution models (MobileNet, YOLOv8-tiny) facilitate real-time head pose estimation and object detection on edge devices without uploading continuous video feeds to external clouds, safeguarding user privacy.

LIT-REF // 03

Multimodal LLM Behavioral Control

Integrating large multimodal models like Google Gemini allows robots to comprehend subtle contextual cues (e.g. distinguishing textbook study from mindless phone scrolling) and synthesize sympathetic, adaptive vocal advice.

DOWNLOAD PDF DRAFT

FocusBot: An Embodied Multimodal Desk Companion Leveraging Edge Vision and Gemini API for Enhanced Student Focus

ABSTRACT // SECTION 1.0 - METHODOLOGY & FINDINGS

Prolonged digital learning environments are notoriously vulnerable to cognitive fatigue and mobile distractions. Traditional mobile lockout applications frequently provoke user resentment or are rapidly uninstalled. In this paper, we introduce FocusBot, a compact desktop robotic platform integrating a 2-DOF pan-tilt vision gimbal, an OLED ocular interface, and a dual-tier cognition pipeline combining edge vision with Google Gemini. By analyzing real-time facial orientation and handheld object classifications, FocusBot assesses cognitive state and applies graduated, non-intrusive physical interventions...

INDEX TERMS — Human-Robot Interaction (HRI), Computer Vision, Gemini API, Embodied AI, Desk Productivity.

[ BILL OF MATERIALS & HARDWARE ARCHITECTURE ]

EQUIPMENTS USED & PINOUT SPECIFICATION

Component breakdown, electrical specifications, and microcontroller pinout assignments.

01 // COMPONENT

Microcontroller Core

ESP32-S3 Dual-Core Xtensa LX7 (240MHz) with 8MB PSRAM & 2.4GHz Wi-Fi / BLE 5.0 for edge orchestration.

02 // COMPONENT

Vision Sensor

OV5640 5MP / USB 1080p 120° Wide-Angle lens module optimized for close-range desktop posture & phone detection.

03 // COMPONENT

Actuators & Gimbal

Dual SG90 / MG90S metal gear micro servos providing 180° horizontal pan and 90° vertical tilt trajectory.

04 // COMPONENT

Displays & Audio

0.96" SSD1306 OLED (128x64 I2C), 12-LED WS2812B NeoPixel ring, INMP441 I2S microphone, and MAX98357A I2S amplifier with 3W speaker.
